name: Case study template
supersedes: v1-proposal — the ten-beat framework (Frame -> Think -> Land), and the interim decision-quad and three-tier-visual-rail proposals, none of which shipped

implementation.note: Sections whose data is absent do not render, so a study can ship partially filled without showing empty headings.

designIntent.readingContract: Scannable in about a minute above the deep dive. Everything an interviewer digs into sits behind a summary rather than competing with the argument.
designIntent.leadEmphasis: Every engagement here was led. The direction/craft split inside the deep dive is what shows the same person set the model and drew the screens — a lead title in the header says nothing about that on its own.
designIntent.positioningSource: Notion — My Archetype (Portfolio planning): operating in ambiguity, prototype in code, consult with engineers mid-build, reduce organizational chaos, scoped the problem, established the framework.

pageFurniture.layout: Single column at every width: title, role byline, tagline, tags, then Employer · Client · Timeframe.
pageFurniture.note: Role is a maroon byline directly under the title — the reader's second question after the project name.

pageFurniture.layout: 32/9 banner, decorative (alt=""), falling back to PlaceholderFigure when a project has no image.
pageFurniture.note: Half the height a 16/9 block gave it. Every substantive visual is a captioned figure further down with its own alt text.
Above the section nav, so a reader deciding whether to read at all hits the figures first. The caveat renders here, once, under the numbers it qualifies.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.purpose: What this was and what I did here, in two to four sentences, plus the project facts that aren't credentials.

sections.heading: The challenge
sections.purpose: What was true before the work, as scannable statements, closing on the reframe that turned a list of problems into a position.
sections.note: Only the `finding` half of each evidence pair renders here. The `response` half belongs to the solution and renders in the deep dive, where findings and the changes they caused sit together.

sections.heading: The solution
sections.purpose: What shipped, as an ordered walk rather than a capability list. Reading the three titles alone should describe the shape of the product.
sections.visuals: A study's own captioned images, or its coded diagrams via section augments, or PlaceholderFigure — so a solution never renders with no picture.
sections.constraint: Two supporting points per step is the ceiling. A third turns the card back into the feature list this section replaced.

sections.heading: Results
sections.purpose: What the work produced: headline, the before/after pair, any business/user/organizational lines, and proof points.
sections.note: metricStatus deliberately does not repeat here — it renders once, in the at-a-glance band.

sections.heading: The deep dive
sections.purpose: The material an interviewer asks about, closed by default.
sections.mechanism: Native <details>. Every route is prerendered and has to stay readable without JS, and the element gives keyboard and screen-reader behaviour for free.

panels.title: Leadership and ownership
panels.purpose: First, because it is the question an interviewer opens with and the one the rest of the page can't answer on its own.
panels.shape: The Direction / Hands on grid leads, then the fuller ownership themes, then the disciplines.

panels.title: The research
panels.purpose: What the research found and the change each finding caused.

panels.title: Edge cases
panels.purpose: Failure designed on purpose, not handled after the fact.

panels.title: Key decisions
panels.purpose: Decisions with their rationale, the path not taken, and what it cost. The strongest senior signal on the page.

panels.title: Reflection
panels.purpose: What was learned, what scale taught, and the transferable principle.

removedPanel.title: What's next
removedPanel.reason: Removed, along with the `nextSteps` field it read from. A roadmap for work that is still moving dates itself faster than anything else on the page.

added.stats: Stat[] — { value, label }. `value` is set in display type, so it stays short. Studies whose outcomes are not numerically verified use a countable design output or a plain word rather than a metric the project record cannot support.
added.overview: string — two to four sentences answering 'what was this, and what did I do here'.
added.leadership: LeadershipPoint[] — { kind: 'Direction' | 'Hands on', title, detail }. Condensed from ownedThemes.
added.visualsPendingNote: string — caption for PlaceholderFigure, saying what the real asset will show.

contentRules: Content strings come from the existing case-study record. Condensing and tightening is allowed; inventing claims is not.
Anything authored is flagged for the owner's sign-off at its site in src/data/caseStudies.ts.
Studies without verified metrics carry countable design outputs in `stats`, never an invented number.
metricStatus renders visibly rather than being hidden — the honest limit is itself a trust signal.
Recreated or stand-in visuals are always labelled as such.
openItems: The condensed copy across all four studies is live but still pending the owner's sign-off — particularly the leadership framing and the `stats` for the three studies without verified metrics.
Per-role accountability lines for analysts, admins, and viewers on finance-cloud.
